land.label: Land, about 10 acres (assumption)
land.assumption: A hypothetical site of about 10 acres with I-10 frontage-road access in the Hankamer segment of the corridor, priced at an assumed $80,000 an acre. The level sits inside the land evidence the research holds for the area: 16.27 acres on SH 61 set back from the interstate asking $995,000, or $61,156 an acre [^2], and 6.82 acres of I-10 frontage at Exit 814 that sold on June 5, 2026 for $482,001 to $552,000 after listing at $668,428 [^1]. Interstate frontage for a truck lot sits toward the top of that range. An appraisal and a contract set the value.

store_site.label: Store, food service, showers, truck lot and site work
store_site.assumption: No construction cost for a Chambers County travel center was found. Published projects run from $10 million for an 11,365 square foot urban travel center (February 2026) [^46] to $18 million for a chain travel center in Illinois with more than 80 truck spaces (November 2024) [^47]; both include costs this line leaves to other lines. The subject is smaller in store and truck lot than either. Construction input prices rose 8.9% in the year to August 2026 [^48], and the county requires new construction 24 inches above base flood elevation [^24], which raises pad costs.

fuel_system.label: Tanks, dispensers and fuel canopies
fuel_system.assumption: No published tank or dispenser cost was found. The line covers underground tanks, gasoline and diesel dispensers and canopies. For scale, a Texas convenience chain budgets $10.0 million to $12.0 million all-in for a large new store with 27 dispensers on 3.7 acres (March 2026) [^44], of which the fuel system is one part.

soft.label: Design, county permits, drainage review and contingency
soft.assumption: County fees are small: a $1,000 drainage deposit, $150 to $450 building permits, $150 per fuel tank and $300 per building for a flammable liquids permit [^23]. The line is mostly design, engineering, drainage and flood work, and a construction contingency.

inventory_wc.label: Opening inventory and working capital
inventory_wc.assumption: Opening store inventory, the first fuel loads and working capital for the ramp. No benchmark was found; the lender sizes it from the operator's purchasing plan.

diesel_gal.label: Diesel gallons
diesel_gal.assumption: No gallons for any Hankamer station were found. An independent travel center offered for sale in September 2025 reported 3.4 million annual gallons, 2.6 million of them diesel, and $2.5 million of inside sales (broker listing, unverified) [^45]. The subject reaches that diesel level by Year 3 on the strength of a truck lot larger than any at the fuel stops between Baytown and Winnie. TxDOT truck counts were not found and are a lender condition.

gas_gal.label: Gasoline gallons
gas_gal.assumption: Reaches the benchmark site's gasoline volume, its 3.4 million total gallons less 2.6 million of diesel, by Year 3 [^45]. Population growth along SH 61 adds local car traffic [^5].

inside_sales.label: Inside sales (store and food)
inside_sales.assumption: Reaches the benchmark site's $2.5 million of inside sales by Year 3 [^45].

diesel_margin.label: Diesel gross margin per gallon
diesel_margin.assumption: A Texas convenience chain earned 43.1 cents a gallon on diesel in fiscal 2025 [^44]. The subject is set below that because Pilot reported lower fuel margins in 2025 [^49] and the chain travel centers 20 miles west compete for fleet fuel.

gas_margin.label: Gasoline gross margin per gallon
gas_margin.assumption: The same chain earned 39.2 cents a gallon on gasoline in fiscal 2025 [^44], and NACS put 2025 retail fuel margins above 40 cents [^43]. The subject is set below both because established branded stations at the SH 61 interchange compete for the same car traffic.

inside_margin.label: Inside gross margin
inside_margin.assumption: The same chain's fiscal 2025 merchandise margin was 35.2% [^44]; the subject is set slightly lower for a new store without a chain's purchasing.

card_fee_cpg.label: Card fees per gallon
card_fee_cpg.assumption: NACS put card fees at 8.4 cents a gallon in 2023 [^53]; the study applies the same charge to diesel and gasoline.

payroll.label: Payroll and benefits, Year 1
payroll.assumption: A 24-hour store with food service and showers. No Chambers County wage data was found. For scale, the same Texas chain reported salaries and benefits of $200.9 million across 448 stores in fiscal 2025 [^44]; the subject runs more services than an average convenience store.

store_opex.label: Utilities, repairs, supplies and marketing, Year 1
store_opex.assumption: Utilities, repairs, supplies and marketing. No travel-center ratio was found; convenience store operating expenses rose 23.3% between 2021 and 2025 [^43].

insurance.label: Property, wind, flood, liability and pollution insurance, Year 1
insurance.assumption: Chambers County is on the Gulf coast; wind and flood premiums were not found, and a quote is a lender condition. The amount is a placeholder for property, wind, flood, liability and pollution cover.

cost_growth.label: Annual growth in payroll and fixed costs
cost_growth.assumption: General allowance; no local cost series was found.

tax_isd.label: Anahuac ISD tax rate, 2024 (2025 assumed unchanged)

tax_tbcd.label: Trinity Bay Conservation District tax rate, 2025

bi_guarantee_pct.label: USDA guarantee share, loans of $5 million to $25 million

bi_fee_pct.label: USDA guarantee fee, share of the guaranteed amount: 3.0% initial plus 0.50% for a guarantee issued before construction is complete

bi_rate.label: All-in rate: note rate plus the annual retention fee
bi_rate.assumption: USDA leaves the rate to lender and borrower [^35]. Prime was 7.00% on October 9, 2026 [^54]. The note rate is assumed at Prime plus 2.00 points for a construction-stage fuel retail loan, and the 0.55% annual retention fee on the 80% guaranteed share [^32] is added on the assumption that the lender passes it to the borrower. The lender sets the rate at pricing

bi_amort_years.label: Amortization
bi_amort_years.assumption: The term may run to the justified useful life of the project or collateral, at most 40 years [^35]. Buildings and paving outlast dispensers and store fixtures; 25 years blends them. The lender must justify the term

bi_equity_min_pct.label: Minimum equity
bi_equity_min_pct.assumption: 7 CFR 5001.105(d), as amended December 11, 2025, sets the equity a new business must show at 20% of its balance sheet, or 25% of project cost, and at 25% for a new business whose guarantee issues before construction is complete [^37]. This travel center is a new business built from the ground up on a guaranteed construction-to-permanent loan, so the model tests 25% of total project cost and charges the fee for a guarantee issued before completion. The lender confirms the measure and the timing of the guarantee at application.

bi_dscr_floor.label: Coverage floor
bi_dscr_floor.assumption: No B&I coverage ratio appears in the rules reviewed; the lender's credit policy governs. The model tests 1.25x in Year 3, the first stabilized year, above SBA's 504 floor because the lender keeps the unguaranteed fifth of the loan.

uses.label: Store, showers, truck lot and site work

opex.label: Property tax
opex.expr: (land + store_site + fuel_system) * (tax_county + tax_isd + tax_tbcd + tax_hospital + tax_nav)
